- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; check for lagged sentiment influence and adjust forecast mid-series.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 10–15 day windows; if forecast deviates >5% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +1.0 followed by -1.0, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 1–2% after sentiment reversal.
